source: Krivov GG, Shapovalov MV, Dunbrack RL Jr. Proteins 2009 Dec;77(4):778-95 PMC2885146
claim: SCWRL4 uses Engh-Huber (1991) ideal geometry for all sidechain coordinate generation from chi angles
evidence: From SCWRL4 paper (PMC2885146) search result: 'uses standard side chain topology based on standard side chain topology (Engh and Huber, 1991) for building the coordinates of all side chain atoms according to rotamer dihedrals.' SCWRL4 is the Dunbrack-lab reference implementation and uses the same Dunbrack 2010 BBDEP library as proxide's source data.
relevance_to_P3_geometry: Direct precedent: the tool most closely aligned with Dunbrack's own library uses Engh-Huber. If proxide matches SCWRL4's geometry source, cross-validation against SCWRL4-placed coordinates is possible.

claim: MSL/MASTER RotamerLibrary is a pure reader with no sidechain coordinate builder; rotlib.bin was pre-built before distribution
evidence: readRotamerLibrary() (mstrotlib.cpp lines 19-134) reads pre-baked binary coords directly from rotlib.bin; no chi-to-Cartesian conversion exists anywhere in the mosaist src tree. grep for 'ideal', 'bond_length', 'nerf', 'Engh', 'CHARMM' in all .cpp files returns zero hits in geometry-relevant context.
relevance_to_P3_geometry: Confirms proxide cannot copy MSL's approach (no builder). The geometry source used to originally build rotlib.bin is not recoverable from source; it is likely Engh-Huber given SCWRL4 precedent but this is an inference gap.

claim: MASTER/MSL backbone-relative frame convention: x=CA-N (N→CA direction), z=x×(C-CA), y=z×x, origin=CA
evidence: mstrotlib.cpp lines 188-194: 'CartesianPoint X = CA - N; CartesianPoint Z = X.cross(C - CA); CartesianPoint Y = Z.cross(X); Frame R(CA, X, Y, Z);'. Proxide frame.rs backbone_frame() implements identical convention with explicit comment 'Matches MSL placeRotamer lines 182–194'.
relevance_to_P3_geometry: CRITICAL: rebuilt coords must live in this exact frame. The P3 geometry engine must place idealized N, CA, C at canonical positions then build in this frame. AC-G round-trip identity test validates this.

claim: CPR r1=1 (Cgamma-exo/UP pucker) chi angles at (-180,-180): chi1=32.5 deg, chi2=-36.0 deg, chi3=25.1 deg, chi4=0; CPR r2=2 (Cgamma-endo/DOWN pucker): chi1=-20.3 deg, chi2=34.0 deg, chi3=-33.8 deg, chi4=0
evidence: Direct read from library: 'CPR  -180 -180     0     1  1  1  0  0.999341    32.5   -36.0    25.1     0.0' and 'CPR  -180 -180     0     2  1  1  0  0.000659   -20.3    34.0   -33.8     0.0'. Pattern is consistent across all phi/psi bins (chi values constant).
relevance_to_P3_geometry: These are the chi values the P3 NeRF builder must reproduce. The sign-alternation pattern (positive chi1, negative chi2, positive chi3 for r1) is the distinguishing signature of the exo pucker. Both puckers must build without CCD correction in the nominal case.

evidence: Direct read: 'PRO  -180 -180     0     1  1  1  0  0.998499    27.3   -34.5    27.8     0.0' and 'PRO  -180 -180     0     2  1  1  0  0.001501   -25.1    36.3   -32.7     0.0'. CPR r1 chi1=32.5 vs PRO r1 chi1=27.3 — a 5.2 deg difference confirming cis-pro needs its own rotamer entry.
relevance_to_P3_geometry: Validates the spec claim that CPR chi differs from PRO chi. AC-R test (3): on real data at (-180,-180), placed cis rotamer chi1 must be closer to 32.5 than 27.3.

source: IUCr International Tables for Crystallography Vol F Ch18.3.2 Table 18.3.2.2; ruppweb.org/Xray/tutorial/engtabl.html
claim: Engh-Huber proline bond geometry: N-CA bond 1.466 Ang (sigma 0.015), N-CA-CB angle 103.0 deg (sigma 1.1 deg), CB-CG-CD angle 106.1 deg (sigma 3.2 deg)
evidence: Search result excerpt from IUCr Table 18.3.2.2: 'N-Calpha (Pro): 1.466 Å (sigma: 0.015). For trans proline: N—CA—CB bond angle is 103.0° with standard deviation 1.1°, and the CB—CG—CD angle is 106.1° with standard deviation 3.2°.' Ruppweb confirms N-CA(Pro)=1.466 Ang.
relevance_to_P3_geometry: These are the exact bond parameter values for the Engh-Huber placeholder in the P3 template. The template builder needs N-CA=1.466, N-CA-CB=103.0 deg, CB-CG-CD=106.1 deg. Full table (CA-CB, CB-CG, CG-CD, CD-N lengths) requires the original Engh-Huber 1991 paper or its IUCr 2001 update for remaining values.

source: Ho BK, Coutsias EA, Seok C, Dill KA. Protein Science 14(4):1011-1018 (2005). PMC2253451
claim: Proline ring exists in two pucker states UP and DOWN; UP has negative chi1 and chi3, positive chi2 and chi4 (opposite for DOWN); endo/exo terminology: Cgamma toward carbonyl = endo; puckers distinguishable by chi sign pattern
evidence: Search result: 'UP characterized by negative chi1 and chi3, positive chi2 and chi4, and DOWN with positive chi1 and chi3, negative chi2 and chi4. Puckering of proline at Cg results in two envelope conformations, the exo and endo ring puckers, based on puckering of the g-carbon toward (endo) or away from (exo) the carbonyl.' CPR r1=(+32.5,-36.0,+25.1) matches DOWN/exo pattern.
relevance_to_P3_geometry: Defines pucker semantics for the P3 builder. r1=1 (CPR chi1=+32.5, chi2=-36.0, chi3=+25.1) is DOWN/exo; r2=2 (chi1=-20.3, chi2=+34.0, chi3=-33.8) is UP/endo. Spec says both must produce geometrically distinct CG positions >= 0.5 Ang apart (AC-G b). The NeRF builder selects endo vs exo by rotamer index r1.

source: Shapovalov MV, Dunbrack RL Jr. Structure 19(6):844-858 (2011). PMC3118414
claim: Dunbrack 2010 BBDEP library contains cis-PRO (CPR) and trans-PRO (PRO/TPR) as separate residue entries with distinct chi distributions; Simple Mode stores all 22 residue types including CPR in one file
evidence: Description.txt from the actual library: '22 residue types = 18 standard amino acids + trans PRO + cis PRO + non-disulfide-bonded CYS and disulfide-bonded CYS.' Also confirmed: CPR has exactly 2 rotamers per bin (r1=1 and r1=2) corresponding to the two ring puckers.
relevance_to_P3_geometry: The P3 engine needs only PRO and CPR templates for v1. The two rotamers per CPR bin ARE the ring puckers; the builder discriminates by rotamer index, not by explicit pucker detection.

source: Engh RA, Huber R. Acta Cryst A47:392-400 (1991); updated in IUCr Int'l Tables Vol F (2001)
claim: Engh-Huber is the de facto standard for ideal amino acid bond lengths and angles used in X-ray structure refinement and is used by SCWRL4, Rosetta, and other major sidechain modeling tools
evidence: Multiple independent sources confirm: SCWRL4 paper cites Engh-Huber 1991 for sidechain topology; Rosetta docs note 'several proline parameters were initially incorrect and have been set to Engh-Huber values'; IUCr standard restraints tables are the Engh-Huber 1991/2001 values. Dunbrack lab BBDEP library documentation references Engh-Huber geometry implicitly via SCWRL4.
relevance_to_P3_geometry: Engh-Huber is the correct baseline for the v1 geometry template. Using it aligns proxide with SCWRL4, which is the reference tool for Dunbrack library coordinates. The spec correctly labels it as a placeholder but it is not a random choice—it is the field standard.

source: Krivov GG, Shapovalov MV, Dunbrack RL Jr. 2009 + Rosetta docs core::conformation::idealization
claim: Rosetta initially had incorrect proline geometry parameters (CD-N-CA angle and others), all subsequently corrected to Engh-Huber values, indicating these values are authoritative and that proline geometry requires careful attention
evidence: Rosetta docs: 'Several proline parameters were initially incorrect, particularly the CD-N-CA angle and other angles/lengths involving the CD-N bond, but these have all been set to their Engh & Huber values.' This flags CD-N bond geometry as an error-prone parameter specifically.
relevance_to_P3_geometry: CD-N bond length (target 1.47 Ang per spec) and CD-N-CA bond angle are the closure-critical parameters. The Rosetta error history confirms these are easy to get wrong. The P3 template must use Engh-Huber values for CD-N-CA angle as the CCD convergence target depends on them.

claim: MSL stores per-rotamer Cartesian coords in a canonical backbone-relative frame and applies a rigid Transform to place them onto actual backbone; there is no chi->Cartesian step at placement time
evidence: placeRotamer() (mstrotlib.cpp:168-233): constructs Frame R from N,CA,C of target residue; constructs Transform T = switchFrames(R, L) from residue frame to lab frame; applies T to stored rotamer coords. The stored coords were built externally before rotlib.bin was shipped. No IC->Cartesian conversion anywhere in rotlib or placement code.
relevance_to_P3_geometry: This confirms Option A (PRECOMPUTED) is correct. The P3 geometry engine runs offline to produce the canonical-frame coords; place_rotamer then applies the same Transform at runtime. The AC-G round-trip identity test verifies this contract is correct.

claim: proxide-geometry NeRF::place_atom is an f32 NeRF (Natural Extension Reference Frame) implementation taking prev_atoms [A,B,C], bond_length, bond_angle_deg, torsion_angle_deg; returns [f32;3]
evidence: nerf.rs line 18: pub fn place_atom(prev_atoms: &[[f32; 3]; 3], bond_length: f32, bond_angle_deg: f32, torsion_angle_deg: f32) -> [f32; 3]. Matches spec §7 statement about f32 signature.
relevance_to_P3_geometry: This is the primitive the P3 geometry engine must use. Chi1=N-CA-CB-CG, chi2=CA-CB-CG-CD, chi3=CB-CG-CD-N define the three NeRF calls needed to place CG, then CD. The f32 precision is acceptable per spec (AC-G tolerance >= 1e-3 Ang).

source: NotebookLM 'proxide: Rotamer Library Theory' (Dunbrack foundational methodology)
claim: The Dunbrack library's sidechain Cartesians are built from library chi + CHARMM residue-topology ideal bond lengths/angles (from minimized Ac-Ala-Xxx-Ala-NHCH3 tetrapeptides), NOT Engh-Huber
evidence: NLM (cited Dunbrack papers): 'bond lengths and angles are obtained from the CHARMM residue topology file ... calculated from minimized tetrapeptides ... all-hydrogen atom parameter set'. (SCWRL4 separately uses Engh-Huber.)
relevance_to_P3_geometry: Refines #820: the FAITHFUL param set to match MASTER/Dunbrack-derived coords is CHARMM, not Engh-Huber. Engh-Huber remains an acceptable v1 placeholder (close ideal geometry) but CHARMM is the convention-matching target.

claim: Proline ring is NOT closed on-the-fly; libraries use two DISCRETE pre-derived pucker clusters selected by chi1 SIGN: chi1>=0 = g+ = Cgamma-ENDO (avg +21/+25 deg); chi1<0 = g- = Cgamma-EXO (avg -20/-25 deg)
evidence: NLM: 'Instead of relying on algorithmic ring-closure kinematics on the fly ... treating the entire ring geometry as belonging to one of two discrete, stable structural clusters (puckers) ... indexed strictly by chi1.' Corrects earlier Ho-et-al mapping: CPR r1 (chi1=+32.5) is g+/Cgamma-ENDO (not exo).
relevance_to_P3_geometry: P3: the canonical method is two fixed pucker templates keyed by chi1 sign, rather than NeRF+CCD. NeRF+CCD can still yield valid closed coords, but a discrete-pucker approach is more faithful and avoids CCD non-convergence. Both puckers (chi1 sign) must build.

source: NotebookLM 'proxide: Rotamer Library Theory' (cites proxide frame.rs + MSL placeRotamer 182-194)
claim: Backbone-relative frame CONFIRMED: origin=CA, x=CA-N, z=x cross (C-CA), y=z cross x (right-handed)
evidence: NLM cited proxide-rotlib frame.rs backbone_frame() and MSL placeRotamer lines 182-194 as matching sources.
relevance_to_P3_geometry: Confirms P3 must build sidechain coords in exactly this frame; AC-G round-trip identity test validates it.
